texts.preamble: Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 In The Court Of Ms. Pooja Aggarwal: Metropolitan Magistrate02 : Mahila Court: South District : Saket Courts: New Delhi Cc No: 189/1 Unique Case Id: 02406R0307522013 Jurisdiction of Police Station: Ambedkar Nagar In the matter of: Smt. Heera Devi, W/o Shri Bhagwan Dass , R/o Dii/314, Madangir, New Delhi, ......................Aggrieved Versus 1) Sh. Bhagwan Dass, 2) Smt Geeta (not summoned) W/o.: Sh Vicky 3) Sh Vicky (not summoned) All R/o Dii/314, Madangir, New Delhi. ..................Respondents Date of Institution : 31.10.2013. Date of Arguments : 18.08.2015 Date of Judgment : 31.08.2015 Exparte Judgment
texts.facts: 1. By way of the present application filed by Smt. Heera Devi (hereinafter referred as ''the aggrieved'') under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against her husband Sh. Bhagwan Dass (hereinafter referred as "the respondent"), the aggrieved has CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 of 12 sought Protection orders under Section 18; Residence Order under Section 19; Monetary Relief under Section 20; and compensation/ damages under Section 22 of the Act. It is pertinent to note that summoning qua the respondent no.2 and respondent no.3 was declined by the Ld Predecessor court vide orders dated 06.11.2013 and 11.07.2014 respectively. 2. Briefly stated, it is the grievance of the aggrieved that she got married to respondent no.1 long ago as per Hindu rites and customs but respondent no. 1 was indifferent, cruel and hostile towards the aggrieved since beginning and being a habitual drunkard, various cruelties, harassment, atrocities, Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/ 1 humiliation, maltreatment, ill treatment, taunting, abuses, beatings and threats to the aggrieved were extended by the respondent which she tolerated in the hope that respondent will mend his ways with the passage of time but to no avail. It is further averred by the aggrieved that even the respondent no. 2 in connivance and collusion with the respondent no. 1 started harassing, humiliating, torturing, abusing and beating the aggrieved as well as her younger daughter Manju. It is further averred that respondent no. 2 even got married to respondent no.3 without permission of the aggrieved/other family members but subsequently the said marriage was accepted. 3. It is further averred that the respondent no. 2 at the instigation and in collusion with respondent no. 3 started harassing, humiliating and torturing and aggrieved as well as her daughter Manju. It is further averred that daughter of aggrieved Manju lodged a complaint with CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 2 of 12 SHO, PS Ambedkar Nagar on 15.10.2013 vide DD No. 49B with respect to the cruelties, harassment, maltreatment, atrocities meted out to her as well as the aggrieved at the hands of the respondent no. 1, 2 and 3. 4. It is also averred that the respondent no. 2 and 3 even after their marriage, frequently visited the house of the aggrieved, used to stay there most of the times and instigated and induced the respondent no. 1 against the aggrieved and Manju and that as and when they visited, they stole costly belongings/household articles from the house and upon protest by the aggrieved, they quarreled with her and also abused her. It is also averred that on 18.10.2013 at night, the aggrieved found some articles were again stolen by respondent no. 2 and 3 and lodged a complaint with SHO, P.S. Ambedkar Nagar on 18.10.2013. 5. It is also the grievance of the aggrieved that she was the owner of a property measuring 100 sq yards, at Narela, New Delhi, which the respondents sold fraudulently in connivance and collusion with each other without her knowledge and permission for a sale consideration amount of Rs. 15,00,000/ which said amount was not given to the aggrieved. It is also averred that the respondents have also harassed the aggrieved and Manju and asked her to vacate the house and they also threatened the aggrieved to dispossess her from the house forcefully if she fails to vacate the house. 6. It is also averred that on 26.10.2013 at about 11.30 am, the respondents in connivance and collusion with each other, forcefully entered into the ground floor of the house where the aggrieved was residing alongwith CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 3 of 12 Manju and started abusing and assaulting the aggrieved and Manju mercilessly and thereafter they forcefully threw them out from the ground floor of the house and that the respondents without having any rights, want to sell and create third party interest in the house after forcefully dispossessing the aggrieved and Manju from the house. 7. It is averred that the aggrieved is presently residing on the top floor of the house under the tin shed alongwith Manju and the respondents have not allowed them to use necessary amenities i.e. bathroom, toilet and to go down stairs and go outside the house for necessary requirement and the respondents have not provided the maintenance and proper food to the aggrieved and Manju.
texts.arguments: It is further averred that the respondent no. 1 never cared nor provided any maintenance to the Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/ 2 aggrieved and her daughter Manju and has deliberately and intentionally neglected and refused to pay maintenance to the aggrieved and that the aggrieved has no other alternative accommodation for her residence and the respondents have forcefully thrown out her from the share household. 8. It has been further averred that the respondent no. 1 is working as Tailor earing Rs. 10000/ per month without any other liability except to maintain the aggrieved which he is not doing despite having sufficient means and income. It has been also averred that the aggrieved has no independent source of income and is dependent upon her parents and on the mercy of relatives. Hence the present case. 9. Notice of the applications was issued to respondent who entered appearance through counsel on 11.07.2014 and filed the reply on behalf of respondent no.1 wherein he did not dispute his marriage to the CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 4 of 12 aggrieved but stated that he was aged about 59 years and suffering from various ailments without any source of income and he has denied working as a tailor now. It was contended therein that the case had been filed only to harass the respondents as it was a false case. All allegations of harassment and cruelty have been denied on merits. He has also stated that the aggrieved shall not be dispossessed from the top floor except in accordance with due process of law. 10. In her replication filed thereto, the aggrieved denied the averments of the respondent no.1 and reaffirmed averments made in her application. 11. Domestic Incident Report was filed by the Protection officer on 30.01.2014. However as respondent did not file his income affidavit despite numerous opportunities nor joined the proceedings despite repeated calls, he was proceeded exparte on 01.06.2015. 12. 15. By virtue of Section 2(a), the reliefs under the Protection of Women CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 5 of 12 From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 can be availed by a woman only if she is in a domestic relationship with the respondent and was subjected to domestic violence by the respondent. 16. The testimony of CW1 in respect of her being married to respondent has not been disputed by the respondent who has rather admitted in his written statement that he got married to the Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/ 3 aggrieved in 1980. Accordingly, by unrebutted testimony, the aggrieved has been able to prove that the CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 6 of 12 respondent has committed certain acts of physical and economic violence against the aggrieved and thus, as the aggrieved person has been able to prove the domestic violence committed upon her, she is entitled to claim reliefs under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondent. Reliefs 18. Protection Order Under Section 18 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act: Aggrieved has prayed for an protection order by prohibiting respondents from entering the school/college/workplace as also prohibiting from respondent(s) from entering the school/college/any other place of her children; Prohibiting respondents from stopping her from going to her school; Prohibiting alienation of assets by the respondent as also directions against the respondent to stay away from the dependents/relatives/any other person of the aggrieved person to prohibit violence against him and also order against the respondents restraining him from indulging from any of the act of domestic violence act defined under section 2 (g) read with section 3 of the Act. 19. 29. The default shall be viewed in terms of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in Gaurav Sondhi Vs. Divya Sondhi-120 DLT(2005)426.
